summary: A metal lantern nobody has built, and the page that explains it. The card's address never changes, so corrections land on the page. What it waits for first is a number off a caliper.
license_note: MIT is what this card's page declares in its #vc-card block ("license": "MIT", read out of the deployed bytes at https://mrdirno.github.io/vibe-cards/moku/ on 2026-08-17), and examples/moku-card/LICENSE is a second MIT copy sitting beside the package. NOTICE at the repo root, served 200 at https://mrdirno.github.io/vibe-cards/NOTICE.txt, withholds artwork for GT-001, Tres Raices, Tierra, Nica, Sala, Manis, Aurea and Bloom, and withholds nothing of this card's: `grep -inE 'moku' NOTICE` returns 3 lines and all three are prose about other entries, none naming a MOKU-003 file. Nothing in this manifest enlarges what NOTICE withholds. The #vc-card block declares replication "open", so this card may be reproduced and sold; the page says the same in words and links its own artwork into Card Studio ready to print. The notice that must travel with a copy is the package's own, whose copyright line reads "Copyright (c) 2026 Compound Crafts — MOKU-003 Mokume Photonic Lattice" — a name that appears nowhere else in this repository except examples/zaria-card/docs/LICENSE, alongside a domain, compound-crafts.io, that does not resolve.
origin: A page-project inside mrdirno/vibe-cards, not a repository of its own and not a fork: the GitHub API reports fork=false and parent=null for that repo, read unauthenticated (x-ratelimit-limit 60), so its MIT is that repo's own grant rather than one inherited from an upstream. THE PACKAGE CAME FROM SOMEWHERE ELSE AND SAYS SO. examples/moku-card/README.md, under "Where it came from": "It was generated somewhere else and handed over as a folder. It did not come from this repository and it is not a fork of anything in it." Its docs/ and tools/ are that folder's own paperwork, kept verbatim — including examples/moku-card/docs/wish-it-better.json, which is NOT this card's manifest and is not live configuration: it declares a mailto at compound-crafts.io and three spinoffs (moku-004-thermal-chandelier, glas-014-mokume-stained-glass, leat-014-mokume-leather-press) that exist nowhere in this repository or on this network. Which generator produced the folder, and whether "Compound Crafts" is a person, a company or a name the generator wrote, is recorded nowhere here. The artwork was drawn by a program rather than photographed — there is no metal anywhere — and examples/moku-card/docs/AUTHORSHIP.md discloses the AI portions (the SDF noise field, the Canvas2D rendering, the asanoha grid maths, the SVG cut export, the QR, and the four python tools) under an EU AI Act Art 50 marking {"ai_generated": true, "card": "MOKU-003"}; no person is depicted. Intake was commit f1266b4, 2026-08-15, titled "The card scanned perfectly and went to a domain that does not exist": the QR and the #vc-card url both read https://compound-crafts.io/cards/MOKU-003, a domain the commit records as having no A, MX, NS or SOA record, so every occurrence was repointed at this page's address and src/site/moku/index.html — this page, written in this repository — shipped in the same commit. Three other things changed at intake: the QR became a marked data-vc-qr image instead of one injected at runtime behind a fallback that did not decode, three preview artifacts stopped printing on the faces, and the wish form came off a dead Supabase project whose key ended fake_anon_key_for_offline_demo. The card took slot 003 of Compound Craft from Carpal Bloom on the owner's instruction, per that same commit.
_note: A page-project's manifest, published at the surface's own url instead of a repo root — the /gt/ shape. The network gate fetches <listed url>/wish-it-better.json, and tools/build_site.py copies everything under src/site/<slug>/ into the artifact, so committing this file serves it at https://mrdirno.github.io/vibe-cards/moku/wish-it-better.json. It is hand-authored on purpose: build_site.py can DERIVE a manifest, but only for entries already in listed[], so a derived one would be produced by the act of listing and criterion 4 would prove itself. GT-001 avoided that by committing its own file before it was listed; this does the same. Measured 2026-08-17 before writing: that url returns 404, the same 9,379-byte body as the host's nonsense-path control. LEVEL IS L0, AND ITS THREE CLAUSES WERE MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. WISH_IT_BETTER.md is present — 15,345 bytes at the repo root, served 200 and byte-identical at https://mrdirno.github.io/vibe-cards/WISH_IT_BETTER.md. The wish channel is this page's own well: the deployed page carries the data-wish-well marker (1 occurrence), which is the marker tools/verify_pages_artifact.mjs requires before it will accept an https channel at all, and it posts to the endpoint in src/site/_wish/config.json, the same well every other card page here uses. A LICENSE exists twice — the GitHub licence API returns spdx_id MIT for the repo's LICENSE, and examples/moku-card/LICENSE is a second MIT beside the package. NOT L1, and it fails both of L1's clauses on this card's own artifacts. (1) "Every shipped change carries an eval meeting §2": examples/moku-card/docs/EVALS.md reports an Instron 68SC slip test and an IR dilatometry run as results — "μ0.34 dry, slip <0.01mm @12N sustained", "measured 0.30±0.02mm" — while examples/moku-card/docs/README.md's own NOT VERIFIED list says the slip test was "not performed in this digital package" and the dilatometry "not measured here; value derived analytically". An eval that reports an unperformed test as performed fails E1 before any other rule gets a turn. The `evals` field above resolves against the repo root, https://github.com/mrdirno/vibe-cards/blob/main/docs/EVALS.md, which is this repo's real eval record and contains zero entries for this card (`grep -ic moku docs/EVALS.md` returns 0). Neither file carries a §2 eval for MOKU-003. (2) "Wishes reach a terminal state": NOT VERIFIED, and not verifiable from outside — the well's anon key is insert-only by design (src/site/_wish/config.json: it "can read nothing back"), and no MOKU-003 wish is recorded anywhere in this repository as claimed, shipped, declined or expired. The queue may work; nothing here shows it did for this card. L2 is nowhere near: it needs an amendment contributed back, and the spec says even its own v1.0.1 "earns nobody L2". WISH_CHANNEL IS THE BARE PAGE URL, NOT <url>/#wish, and that is deliberate. build_site.py's derived manifests declare {slug}/#wish, but src/site/moku/index.html contains no element with id="wish" — 0 matches in the source and 0 in the deployed page — and the gate strips the fragment before fetching, so a #wish landing nowhere would never be caught by the check that reads this field. The route a card holder actually has is the form on this page. WHAT THIS FILE DOES NOT ESTABLISH. Nobody has built the object, so no measurement decides the 0.30 mm the package claims a cell opens against the 0.0576 mm the page's own arithmetic gives from the same rule. No wish was posted to prove the well accepts one: the 13-lane audit that did that on this network put two probe rows into a live queue and owed the cleanup, so this pass read the deployed bytes instead. The physical card exists as a ledger row, not a read-back — src/site/network.json records MOKU-003's chip write as LEDGER-DERIVED, meaning the url on this file's own card was recorded as written and has never been read back off the tag.
